name: Battling Ring Angels Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Nicknamed “BRATT” by the fed's own commentary, first contested in January 2000 between Jenny Anderson and the team of Simply Divine; by the promotion's final 2001 season the belts were on the line between the site's own British Bombshells and East/West, an outcome the surviving record does not confirm.

name: Battling Ring Angels Celestial Championship
epitaph: BRA's own top singles title, changing hands repeatedly across the promotion's run (Sherry Ann, Yvette Malreaux, Evonne Carmikel, Lisa Dream, Tiffany Lane and Lindsay Locke among its recorded holders); a 2001 “Celestial Tournament” closes out the surviving record with a Heaven-and-Hell cage final between Akira Hagawa and Casey Gaines whose result does not survive.

name: Battling Ring Angels Television Championship
epitaph: Created in January 2000 and first won by Tiffany Epitaphine in a ladder match with the belt suspended above the ring, per the fed's own news column; later challengers included Americana and Nina Larue.

name: Battling Ring Angels Featherweight Championship
epitaph: A weight-class title whose belt Jennifer Christian won from Angel Dust on 16 October 2000 and lost by the site's own next mention of the division, in December 2000; a 2001 tournament for the vacant title (Jenn Christian, Shea London, Tiffany Lane, Sissy Landers among the entrants) closes out the surviving record unresolved.

name: Battling Ring Angels Hardcore Championship
epitaph: A no-rules title contested repeatedly through 2000 among wrestlers including Janus and Sandra “The Tiger” Blake; not confirmed on the belt of any wrestler minted from this pass's own roster.

name: Battling Ring Angels Fallen Angel Championship
epitaph: Won by Lesley “Viper” Magnus from Janus on 2 October 2000 in an “I quit” match and defended successfully against Sasha and again against Janus through the end of the surviving record.

name: Battling Ring Angels Women's Middleweight Championship
epitaph: A weight-class belt the fed's own year-end pay-per-view introduced vacant, contested and won in the same broadcast; the surviving record holds no history for it before that night.
